# eindir

> eindir is a Rust crate, eindir-core, with Python, C and C++ bindings. It has the primitives for bounded optimisation and sampling on R^D: the Objective trait, box bounds, Halton point sets, gradients, a GLE coloured-noise thermostat and surrogate models. The anneal optimiser is built on it.

Each link points at the Org source of a page under `docs/orgmode/` on GitHub. The site, https://eindir.rgoswami.me/, is built from the same sources by Sphinx, and `llms-full.txt` has every page as Markdown in one file.

The Python package is narrower than the Rust crate. `eindir` exports `NumLimit`, `FPair`, `ObjectiveFunction`, `OutOfBounds`, `low_discrepancy_points`, `styblinski_tang` and array API, DLPack and TVM-FFI helpers, and `eindir._core` adds `Bounds`, `PyObjective` and `shifted_low_discrepancy_points`. `GleThermostat`, `optimal_sampling_drift`, `matrix_exp`, `ldl_sqrt`, `halton_unit`, the surrogates, the gradient adapters and the builtin objective types are Rust-only. CI runs the Python blocks of the manual, and the Rust code in the tutorials is included from `examples/`.

The `eindir-python` skill and the three others under `skills/` give worked examples of common tasks, with scripts that CI runs. `AGENTS.md` has the build, test and documentation commands and the mistakes that are easy to make. Both are reproduced at the end of `llms-full.txt`.

## Tutorials

- [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/index.org): What eindir provides, its bindings, the pages to read first, and how to cite it.
- [Quickstart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/quickstart.org): Evaluate a function at eight Halton points in a box, from Python and from Rust, with the output of each.
- [Tutorials](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/tutorials.org): The tutorials, what each covers, and how to print the installed version.
- [Quickstart with Python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/tutorials/quickstart.org): Wrap a Python function and its gradient as an objective, draw start points, and use the pure-Python NumLimit and ObjectiveFunction.
- [Low-discrepancy points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/tutorials/low-discrepancy.org): Halton points from Python and Rust: plain designs, skip, seeded shifted replicas and corner-anchored designs.
- [GLE thermostat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/tutorials/gle-thermostat.org): Build the GLE thermostat with the optimal-sampling drift, start it at equilibrium and check the momentum variance, in Rust.
- [Surrogates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/tutorials/surrogates.org): Fit an additive surrogate on a Halton pilot, draw proposals from it, and search along one direction with a reduced objective, in Rust.

## How-to Guides

- [Installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/howto/install.org): Install from PyPI or crates.io, build the Python package or the C library from source, and use the pixi environments.
- [Gradients](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/howto/gradients.org): Give an objective a gradient in Rust (by hand, closure, forward-mode AD or central differences), in Python with grad_fn, and in C.
- [Objectives through the C ABI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/howto/c-objective.org): Install the C library, check the ABI stamp, write value and gradient callbacks, create or embed a handle, report failures with a message, and wrap the handle in Rust, with a complete C program.
- [Objectives that can fail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/howto/fallible.org): Write an objective that returns errors, pass them through a generic driver unchanged, and turn them into NaN for infallible code, with a complete Rust program.
- [Using with anneal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/howto/using-with-anneal.org): Which eindir items the anneal drivers use for the objective, start points, GLE moves and surrogate proposals.
- [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/howto/faq.org): ImportError from old examples, gradients, use without anneal, TypeError and PanicException from Python, C and C++ use, the licence (MIT) and how to cite eindir.

## Explanation

- [The primitives](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/explanation/primitives.org): The objective and bounds traits and how the point sets, gradients, GLE thermostat, surrogates and bindings relate to them.
- [Low-discrepancy point sets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/explanation/low-discrepancy.org): Why Halton points, how the radical inverse builds them, Cranley-Patterson shifts and corner-anchored designs, with references.
- [The GLE thermostat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/explanation/gle.org): What the GLE thermostat computes, why the covariance fixes correctness while the drift sets the speed, the fitted optimal-sampling drift, with references.
- [Surrogates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/explanation/surrogates.org): The additive Chebyshev surrogate and its backfitting, independence proposals corrected by the true objective, and reduced objectives on an active subspace, with references.
- [Fallible objectives](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/explanation/fallible-objectives.org): The TryObjective, TryGradient and TryDifferentiableObjective traits with a caller-chosen error type, their blanket impls for infallible objectives, the adapters, the C status-and-message callbacks, and how a driver should carry the error.
- [The C ABI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/explanation/c-abi.org): The two C handles, the ABI stamp and its compatibility rule, the semantic descriptor and its wildcards, the DLPack tensor rules, error reporting and the Rust wrappers.
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/architecture.org): The repository layout, the three crate types (rlib, cdylib, staticlib), how the Python, C and C++ bindings are produced, and where the version lives.

## Reference

- [Python API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/reference/api-primitives.org): Every name in eindir and eindir._core with its signature, the argument types and exceptions, and the list of Rust-only items.
- [C API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/reference/c-api.org): Every function, type and constant of eindir-core.h: version and compatibility, errors, both handles, the descriptor, tensor rules and the Rust wrappers.
- [Rust API Reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/reference/rust-api.org): The entry page of the Rust API reference that Sphinx generates from the doc comments of the crate.
- [Glossary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/reference/glossary.org): Short definitions of the terms the manual uses, from ABI stamp to TryObjective.
- [Bindings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/bindings.org): How the Python wheel, the C library with its header and pkg-config file, and the C++ header are built, with Meson and CMake snippets for consumers.

## Development

- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/contributing.org): Setup, commit types, towncrier fragments, the single version source in Cargo.toml, style, tests and the documentation checks.
- [Best Practices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/docs/orgmode/dev/best_practices.org): Define the objective once, use low-discrepancy starts, reuse the GLE drift, accept surrogate proposals with the true objective, and keep arrays on their device.
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/AGENTS.md): Build, test and documentation commands, common tasks and pitfalls for working in this repository.

## Skills

- [eindir-c-abi](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/skills/eindir-c-abi/SKILL.md): Build and install the eindir C library, link C or C++ programs to it, and define objectives in C with DLPack 1.0 tensors that Rust drivers can call. Use when compiling against eindir-core.h or eindir-core.hpp, writing eval or gradient callbacks, embedding eindir_objective_t in another library's struct, checking ABI compatibility or semantic descriptors, or when a program fails to start because libeindir_core.so.0.8 is missing.
- [eindir-contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/skills/eindir-contributing/SKILL.md): Prepare a change to eindir for review. Covers which files to edit for code, the C ABI, the manual and the version, the commit types cog accepts, towncrier fragments, the Org to Sphinx docs build, regenerating llms.txt, and bumping the version from Cargo.toml. Use before committing to eindir, when the lint, version-drift or skills CI jobs fail, or when preparing a release.
- [eindir-python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/skills/eindir-python/SKILL.md): Use the eindir Python package to build box bounds, wrap a Python function and optionally its gradient as an objective, and draw bounded Halton (low-discrepancy) start points, through eindir and its Rust extension eindir._core. Says which names exist in Python and which are Rust-only (the generalized Langevin equation (GLE) thermostat, the surrogates, the gradient adapters, the builtin objective types), and which argument types and exceptions trip callers up. Use when writing Python against eindir, when an example from the eindir manual fails with ImportError, or when an eindir call raises TypeError or PanicException.
- [eindir-rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HaoZeke/eindir/main/skills/eindir-rust/SKILL.md): Write Rust against the eindir-core crate. Implement the Objective trait on box Bounds, draw Halton start points, evaluate batches in parallel, and supply gradients (analytic, central finite differences or forward-mode autodiff). Covers the builtin test objectives, the generalized Langevin equation (GLE) thermostat with coloured noise built from the optimal-sampling drift, and fitting and sampling the additive Chebyshev surrogate. Use for the GLE thermostat and the surrogates, which have no Python binding, when the eindir manual's Python examples for them fail, or when eindir-core does not build or panics.
